text:
michelle: Heads-up — Lyncrest just sent their LoRA merge + int4 quant artifacts for onboarding. Quick smoke run shows lower latency but some QA/summary outputs are terser and a handful of hallucinations. Dropping the quick numbers here.

michelle: Upload: s3://redwood-cust-artifacts/lyncrest/merge_2024-05-03.tar.gz
michelle: Eval pack: gs://redwood-evals/lyncrest/quickpack_v1.tar.gz

devin: grabbing the pack now. which baseline did they merge against? fp16 or int8?

michelle: baseline is fp16-candidate-20240411. They applied a LoRA on top and we ran post-merge quant to int4 with our standard calibration.

samir: quick run on a 50-sample QA + summaries subset:
```
# run: py eval/quick_eval.py --model lyncrest/merged:int4 --cases 50 --out /tmp/lyn_q.json
# results snippet
perplexity: 12.4 -> 15.9 (baseline -> merged:int4)
QA EM: 84.2 -> 80.7 (-3.5 pts)
ROUGE-L (summaries): 0.42 -> 0.38
we saw 6 hallucinated entity facts in the 50 examples (not huge but noticeable)
```

samir: also noticed that a token alias in their tokenizer maps U+2019 -> ' (smart quote -> apostrophe) got lost after merging, so some contractions are tokenized differently.

devin: can you paste the tokenizer diff? that mapping loss could lead to shift in probabilities.

samir: small diff:
```
- mapping: 0x2019 -> 39
+ mapping: 0x2019 -> 8212
# so smart-quote now becomes 2 tokens in a few cases
```

michelle: that aligns with the terser outputs — broken tokenization + int4 quantization causing different logit shapes for ngram boundaries.

sara: I can run targeted prompt-sensitivity tests (dates, amounts, customer names) and surface worst-offending prompts. Putting a job in the queue.

devin: I'll re-run calibration with our alternate bit-slicing kernel (quant-calib v2) and see if that recovers EM. If not, we should try a hybrid where kv-cache remains fp16.

michelle: good. Propose plan:
1) sara: targeted prompt suite, produce top-10 regressions by relative drop (due EOD).
2) devin: try quant-calib v2 + fp16-kvcache hybrid smoke (2h).
3) samir: produce tokenizer remap patch for smart-quote -> map back to single token, run small smoke.
4) If regressions < 2% overall or hallucinations < 1% of responses, canary to 10% on dedicated pool with rollback hooks.

merge-bot: PR #4821 merged into lyncrest/merged (summary: apply lora weights + int4 quant artifacts). :white_check_mark:

devin: quick note — when you canary, use route policy: region=us-west & fallback=fp16-baseline. That way traffic auto-fails to baseline on SLO breach.

ops-bot: Canary policy created: name=lyncrest-canary-10pct, timeout=120s, fallback_model=fp16-candidate-20240411

sara: starting prompt runs now. I see some systematic drop on prompts containing parentheses and date formats. Possibly token boundary issue too. Will push CSV with examples.

samir: remap patch is small, testing locally. If remap + alt-calib reduces EM drop to <1.5 pts, we should be safe to canary.

michelle: timeline check — aim for canary by tomorrow 1500 UTC. If anything looks worse in canary, auto-rollback is enabled and we'll open a postmortem.

devin: noted. I'll also capture per-token entropy deltas to help identify whether quant noise is concentrated at boundaries or uniformly distributed.

sara: uploaded worst-10 CSV: s3://redwood-debug/lyncrest/worst10_1744443210.csv

michelle: thanks. Assigning owners: sara (regression examples + report), devin (quant calibrations + canary job), samir (tokenizer remap + small patch PR). I'll follow up with customer-facing note after canary pass.

samir: small update — remap PR posted: https://git.internal.redwood/lyncrest/tokenizer/PR-77

michelle: perfect. Everyone ping me on this thread with any blocking logs. :thumbsup:

devin: FYI — if we need to, we can deploy a model-variant that keeps attention & kv in fp16 while quantizing only the feedforward matmuls. Lower perf hit but often fixes these edge regressions.

michelle: good fallback. calling this out in the canary runbook.

sara: running final smoke now (after remap + alt-calib). will report in ~30m.

michelle: thanks — appreciated.
